In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of Tax-induced activation of the HTLV- 1 promoter.
the mechanisms of transcriptional activation mediated by the HTLV- 1 Tax protein.
the mechanism by which HTLV-1 transactivation occurs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HTLV- 1 Tax protein interacts with the CREB transcriptional activator and CREB binding protein, a coactivator, to stimulate viral transcription.
Tax recruits CBP to the viral promoter, and that this recruitment is a critical step in the activation process.
Tax promotes the high-affinity binding to CREB-virus CRE complex by CBP, which increases the stability of the nucleoprotein complex and results in strong transcriptional activation of HTLV- 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tax promotes high affinity binding of KIX to viral CRE complexes by up to ~4.4 kcal/mole.
Tax promotes high affinity binding of the Kix domain of CBP to CREB-virus CRE complexes and this interaction is essential for Tax to transactivate HTLV-1.

HTLV-1 Tax recruits CBP to the Tax-responsive CRE in the viral promoter through a direct interaction between the KIX domain on CBP and the basic leucine-zipper domain of CREB, resulting in strong transcriptional activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HTLV-1 Tax protein is a potent activator of HTLV- 1 transcription through its ability to anchor the cellular coactivator, CBP, to the viral promoter.
HTLV-1 Tax protein is able to recruit the transcription factor CREB to the HTLV1 LTR and then recruit the co-activator CBP through its KIX domain.
